'''''Napoleon''''' is a 2023 [[Epic film|epic]] [[Historical drama|historical]] [[war film]] directed and co-produced by [[Ridley Scott]] from a screenplay by [[David Scarpa]]. Based on the life of [[Napoleon]] and primarily depicting his rise to power, as well as his relationship with his wife, [[Joséphine de Beauharnais|Joséphine]], it stars [[Joaquin Phoenix]] as Napoleon and [[Vanessa Kirby]] as Joséphine.

In October 2020, Scott announced ''Napoleon'' as his next project. Following delays and recastings due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], filming began in February 2022 in [[England]], lasting several months. In addition to writer David Scarpa, frequent Scott collaborators included cinematographer [[Dariusz Wolski]] and editor [[Claire Simpson]].

''Napoleon'' premiered at [[Salle Pleyel]] in Paris on November 14, 2023, and was released in the United States and United Kingdom on November 22 by [[Columbia Pictures]] (via [[Sony Pictures Releasing]])<!-- Apple TV+ is NOT a theatrical distributor --> before streaming on [[Apple TV+]] on March 1, 2024. The film grossed $222.4{{nbsp}}million worldwide, becoming a [[box office bomb|box office disappointment]] though it performed slightly better overseas, and received mixed reviews from critics, who praised the battle sequences and performances but criticized its tone, pacing, and historical inaccuracies. At the [[96th Academy Awards]], the film received nominations for [[Academy Award for Best Production Design|Best Production Design]], [[Academy Award for Best Costume Design|Best Costume Design]], and [[Academy Award for Best Visual Effects|Best Visual Effects]].

==Plot==
<!--- PLOTS ARE GENERALLY 400-700 WORDS; CURRENT COUNT: 596 -->
In 1793, amid the [[French Revolution]], young army officer [[Napoleon Bonaparte]] watches [[Marie Antoinette]] beheaded by the [[guillotine]]. Later that year, Revolutionary leader [[Paul Barras]] has Napoleon manage the [[Siege of Toulon (1793)|Siege of Toulon]]; he storms the enemy fort and repels the British ships with artillery. After [[Maximilien Robespierre]] is [[Fall of Maximilien Robespierre|deposed and executed]] at the end of the [[Reign of Terror]], French leaders, including Napoleon, attempt to restore stability. Again employing artillery, Napoleon suppresses the royalist insurrection on [[13 Vendémiaire]] in 1795.

Napoleon woos aristocratic widow [[Joséphine de Beauharnais]] and the two eventually marry. Despite their vigorous sex life, they bear no children. In [[Ottoman Egypt|Egypt]], he prevails again at the [[Battle of the Pyramids]] in 1798, but rushes home when he hears Joséphine has an almost 10-year younger lover, [[Hippolyte Charles]]. The [[French Directory|Directory]] criticises him for abandoning his troops, but he condemns them for their poor leadership of France and with several collaborators such as [[Charles Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord|Talleyrand]], [[Joseph Fouché|Fouché]], [[Emmanuel Joseph Sieyès|Sieyès]] and [[Roger Ducos|Ducos]], overthrows them in the [[Coup of 18 Brumaire]] and becomes [[First Consul]].

Napoleon is [[Coronation of Napoleon and Joséphine|crowned]] [[Emperor of the French]] by the [[Pope Pius VII|pope]] in 1804, during which he audaciously puts the crown on his own head. Foreign Minister Talleyrand suggests to [[Austrian Empire|Austria]] an alliance, though the Austrians dismiss the idea. A year later, Napoleon outmanoeuvres and defeats the Austrians and the Russians at the [[Battle of Austerlitz]], forcing them to retreat over frozen lakes before bombarding the ice and drowning them. Afterwards, he invites Austrian Emperor [[Francis II, Holy Roman Emperor|Francis II]] for wine—which Russian Tsar [[Alexander I of Russia|Alexander I]] declines to attend—and tells Francis that since he did not totally destroy their armies, he expects the latter to be grateful.

[[Letizia Bonaparte|Napoleon's mother]] has him impregnate a mistress, proving that Joséphine is infertile. He divorces her in 1810, publicly slapping her in the face when she initially refuses to read her portion of the decree, but the two remain on good terms and continue exchanging friendly letters. Napoleon marries [[Marie Louise, Duchess of Parma|Marie Louise of Austria]], who bears [[Napoleon II|a son]] one year later.

In 1812, Napoleon [[French invasion of Russia|invades Russia]] after Alexander reneges on the [[Treaties of Tilsit]]. He prevails, despite bloody guerrilla resistance by [[Don Cossacks]], and then fighting the huge [[Battle of Borodino]], but finds [[Moscow]] empty and later [[Fire of Moscow (1812)|set aflame]]. Napoleon retreats during the winter to France, having lost about half a million men. In 1814, the [[Sixth Coalition|Coalition]] forces Napoleon's abdication and exiles him to [[Elba]].

In 1815, upon hearing that Joséphine is unwell, Napoleon escapes the island and in the [[Hundred Days]] returns to power in France. She, having been forced into reclusion at the [[Château de Malmaison]], dies before he arrives. King [[Louis XVIII]] sends the Fifth Regiment to stop Napoleon, but he charms them into joining him.

At the [[Battle of Waterloo]] in June, Napoleon, having amassed more troops, confronts the [[British Army|British army]] under [[Arthur Wellesley, 1st Duke of Wellington|Arthur Wellesley, Duke of Wellington]]. French cavalry charges are repulsed by British [[infantry square]]s, and a desperate Napoleon urges his remaining soldiers forward, but this advance is defeated by re-formed lines of enemy infantry. The forces of [[Prussia]]n [[Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher|Marshal Blücher]] arrive to reinforce Wellesley, and the French are broken. As Napoleon retreats, he salutes Wellesley.

Napoleon is exiled, this time to the island of [[Saint Helena]] in the middle of the [[Atlantic Ocean]], and is seen bantering with children, writing his [[The Memorial of Saint Helena|memoirs]] that would become read all over the world and presenting to his listeners a version of history where he is always right. An unwell Napoleon collapses, hearing Joséphine beckon him to meet her again. Napoleon dies in 1821. An epilogue notes that roughly 3 million people died in his wars.

==Production==
===Development===
[[File:NASA Journey to Mars and “The Martian” (201508180030HQ).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Director Scott in 2015]]
On October 14, 2020, the same day his film ''[[The Last Duel (2021 film)|The Last Duel]]'' (2021) wrapped filming, [[Ridley Scott]] announced ''Napoleon'', at that point provisionally called ''Kitbag'', as his next project for [[20th Century Studios]], based on [[Napoleon]]'s life. He would direct and produce, while the screenplay was written by Scott's ''[[All the Money in the World]]'' (2017) collaborator [[David Scarpa]]. The film's working title was derived from the saying that "There is a general's staff hidden in every soldier's kitbag".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Busch |first=Jenna |date=January 20, 2022 |title=Bye Bye Kitbag: Ridley Scott Very Wisely Renames His Napoleon Movie |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/740141/bye-bye-kitbag-ridley-scott-very-wisely-renames-his-napoleon-movie/ |access-date=December 31, 2023 |website=[[/Film]] |language=en-US |archive-date=December 31, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231231153427/https://www.slashfilm.com/740141/bye-bye-kitbag-ridley-scott-very-wisely-renames-his-napoleon-movie/ |url-status=live }}</ref> During the same year, Scott also consulted with [[University of Oxford]] scholar Michael Broers regarding Napoleon's life, particularly collaborating with him in deconstructing the geography of the [[Battle of Waterloo]]. He also received [[Stanley Kubrick]]'s script for his planned Napoleon film, which never materialized.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Schulman |first=Michael |date=November 6, 2023 |title=Ridley Scott's "Napoleon" Complex |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2023/11/13/ridley-scott-director-profile |url-access=limited |access-date=January 25, 2024 |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |language=en-US |issn=0028-792X}}</ref> By January 2021, [[Apple Studios]] announced its commitment to finance and produce the film, with filming scheduled to begin in the United Kingdom in 2022.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fleming |first=Mike Jr. |date=January 14, 2021 |title=Apple Studios Commits to ''Kitbag'', Ridley Scott-Directed Epic with Joaquin Phoenix as French Conqueror Napoléon Bonaparte |url=https://deadline.com/2021/01/napoleon-movie-joaquin-phoenix-ridley-scott-apple-studios-kitbag-1234672742/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114160718/https://deadline.com/2021/01/napoleon-movie-joaquin-phoenix-ridley-scott-apple-studios-kitbag-1234672742/ |archive-date=January 14, 2021 |access-date=November 22, 2021 |website=Deadline Hollywood}}</ref>

===Writing===
Scarpa had been approached by Scott to write a film based on Napoleon following production of ''All the Money in the World''. As he initially had a "high school basic knowledge" of his life, he researched Napoleon and after realizing that writing a film encompassing his entire life was impractical, he decided to focus on Napoleon's relationship with his wife, Josephine.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Anne |date=December 2, 2023 |title=Ridley Scott's 'Napoleon': Writer David Scarpa Explains What's True and False |url=https://www.indiewire.com/awards/consider-this/ridley-scott-napoleon-writer-david-scarpa-true-false-1234931486/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231202181026/https://www.indiewire.com/awards/consider-this/ridley-scott-napoleon-writer-david-scarpa-true-false-1234931486/ |archive-date=December 2, 2023 |access-date=January 26, 2024 |website=[[IndieWire]]}}</ref> He began by reading ''Napoleon: A Concise Biography'' by [[David A. Bell]], but did not understand it, read more books and watched YouTube videos. When researching Josephine, he cited ''Ambition and Desire: The Dangerous Life of Josephine Bonaparte'' by [[Kate Williams (historian)|Kate Williams]] as his primary influence.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zacharias |first=Ramona |date=January 8, 2024 |title=What Is The Napoleon Complex? David Scarpa Discusses His Titular Film |url=https://www.creativescreenwriting.com//what-is-the-napoleon-complex-david-scarpa-discusses-his-titular-film |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240126022106/https://www.creativescreenwriting.com/what-is-the-napoleon-complex-david-scarpa-discusses-his-titular-film/ |archive-date=January 26, 2024 |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=Creative Screenwriting}}</ref> He took inspiration from Scott's ''[[The Duellists]]'' (1977) and [[Miloš Forman|Milos Forman]]'s ''[[Amadeus (film)|Amadeus]]'' (1984), wanting to portray Napoleon as an "irreverent" figure similar to how Mozart was depicted in ''Amadeus'', and told Scott he envisioned Napoleon as being competent "in the realm of battle", and "incompetent in the realm of love". Scott proposed the idea of beginning the film with Marie Antoinette being under the guillotine, wanting to focus on the "ambivalence about where democracy leads".<ref name=":1" /> Scott's writing process also involved hand-drawing [[storyboard]]s, with him sending Scarpa the illustrations once Scarpa sent him pages from the script.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Lane |date=November 21, 2023 |title=Recreating Napoleon's Biggest, Baddest Trap |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/napoleon-ridley-scott-battle-of-austerlitz-behind-the-scenes.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231122030941/https://www.vulture.com/article/napoleon-ridley-scott-battle-of-austerlitz-behind-the-scenes.html |archive-date=November 22, 2023 |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]}}</ref>

In August 2024, it was reported that Phoenix had threatened to leave the film unless [[Paul Thomas Anderson]] (with whom Phoenix previously worked on ''[[The Master (2012 film)|The Master]]'' and ''[[Inherent Vice (2014 film)|Inherent Vice]]'') was recruited to rewrite the script. Eventually, the situation calmed down and Phoenix remained involved in the production.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/joaquin-phoenix-drops-out-movie-1235973446/|title=Joaquin Phoenix's Last-Minute Exit Sparks "Huge Amount of Outrage" Among Hollywood Producers|website=The Hollywood Reporter|first1=Kim|last1=Masters|first2=Mia|last2=Galuppo|first3=Borys|last3=Kit|date=August 13, 2024|access-date=August 17, 2024}}</ref> Later that year, Scott confirmed that Anderson had indeed been brought in for rewrites, saying: "It turned into a lot of fun, actually. Three of us in this room screaming with laughter."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/ridley-scott-paul-thomas-anderson-rewrote-napoleon-1235063592/|title=Ridley Scott Confirms Paul Thomas Anderson Was Brought in to Re-Write 'Napoleon'|first=Harrison|last=Richlin|website=[[IndieWire]]|date=November 7, 2024|access-date=November 7, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/film/joaquin-phoenix-threatened-quit-napoleon-paul-thomas-anderson-rewrite-script-3811501|title=Joaquin Phoenix threatened to quit 'Napoleon' until Paul Thomas Anderson came on board to rewrite the script|first=Max|last=Pilley|website=[[NME]]|date=November 11, 2024|access-date=November 11, 2024}}</ref> Anderson confirmed his involvement with the script rewrites in September 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thewrap.com/paul-thomas-anderson-killers-of-the-flower-moon-napoleon-rewrites/|title=Paul Thomas Anderson Confirms Rumor He Helped on 'Killers of the Flower Moon,' 'Napoleon' Rewrites|first=Casey|last=Loving|website=[[TheWrap]]|date=September 24, 2025|access-date=September 24, 2025}}</ref>

===Casting===
[[Joaquin Phoenix]] was reportedly attached to star as the French general and emperor [[Napoléon]], reuniting him with the director after ''[[Gladiator (2000 film)|Gladiator]]'' (2000).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2020/10/ridley-scott-joaquin-phoenix-napoleon-epic-kitbag-wraps-the-last-duel-today-1234597342/|title=Ridley Scott Eyes Another Epic: Joaquin Phoenix as Napoleon in ''Kitbag'' as Director Today Wraps ''The Last Duel''|date=October 14, 2020|first=Mike Jr.|last=Fleming|website=Deadline Hollywood|access-date=November 22, 2021|archive-date=October 15, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201015054250/https://deadline.com/2020/10/ridley-scott-joaquin-phoenix-napoleon-epic-kitbag-wraps-the-last-duel-today-1234597342/|url-status=live}}</ref> Scott had Phoenix and another actor in mind to play Napoléon, but felt "blown away" by Phoenix's performance as the [[Joker (character)|titular character]] in ''[[Joker (2019 film)|Joker]]'' (2019) and, despite disliking how that film apparently celebrated violence, concluded that Phoenix could be an "amazing asset" for ''Napoleon'', both creatively and commercially.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2023/10/ridley-scott-napoleon-joaquin-phoenix-casting-joker-gladiator-1235566587/|title=Ridley Scott On Capturing Epic 'Napoleon' & Why He Chose Joaquin Phoenix To Play The Emperor – Contenders London|date=October 7, 2023|first=Andreas|last=Wiseman|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231007230119/https://deadline.com/2023/10/ridley-scott-napoleon-joaquin-phoenix-casting-joker-gladiator-1235566587/|archive-date=October 7, 2023|url-status=live|access-date=October 8, 2023}}</ref>

''The Last Duel'' actress [[Jodie Comer]] was reportedly Scott's first choice to play Joséphine. She entered negotiations to star in March 2021, confirmed her casting in September, and said: "I just jumped at the chance to work with Ridley and his team again and the idea of working with Joaquin, who's someone who I hugely admire... I'm so excited to delve into that world."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2021/03/jodie-comer-josephine-joaquin-phoenix-apple-ridley-scotts-napoleon-kitbag-1234704485/|title=Jodie Comer Is Ridley Scott's Choice To Play Josephine Opposite Joaquin Phoenix In Napoléon Bonaparte Pic ''Kitbag'' For Apple Studios|date=March 2, 2021|first=Justin|last=Kroll|website=Deadline Hollywood|access-date=November 22, 2021|archive-date=May 23, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220523141857/https://deadline.com/2021/03/jodie-comer-josephine-joaquin-phoenix-apple-ridley-scotts-napoleon-kitbag-1234704485/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2021/film/news/jodie-comer-ridley-scott-kitbag-1235054668/|title=''Killing Eve'' Star Jodie Comer Confirmed for Ridley Scott's ''Kitbag'' Opposite Joaquin Phoenix|date=September 3, 2021|first=K.J.|last=Yossman|website=Variety|access-date=November 22, 2021|archive-date=March 31, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220331090738/https://variety.com/2021/film/news/jodie-comer-ridley-scott-kitbag-1235054668/|url-status=live}}</ref> In November, she said her role was "going to be another huge challenge, but what I love about period dramas is that kind of transformation. Even now, doing some costume and hair tests for ''Kitbag'', it's just so exciting because it becomes so much easier to step out of yourself and into somebody else."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2021/tv/global/jodie-comer-killing-eve-adam-driver-last-duel-1235106912/|title=Jodie Comer on Closing the Chapter on Villanelle, Owning Her Place on ''Last Duel'' and Making Her West End Debut|date=November 8, 2021|first=Manori|last=Ravindran|website=Variety|access-date=November 22, 2021|archive-date=November 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122154334/https://variety.com/2021/tv/global/jodie-comer-killing-eve-adam-driver-last-duel-1235106912/|url-status=live}}</ref> The same month, [[Youssef Kerkour]] was confirmed to star.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goldenglobes.com/articles/youssef-kerkour-house-gucci-and-challenging-typecasting|title=Youssef Kerkour on ''House of Gucci'' and Challenging Typecasting|date=November 23, 2021|first=Raffi|last=Boghosian|publisher=Golden Globes|access-date=March 14, 2022|archive-date=January 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220107175011/https://www.goldenglobes.com/articles/youssef-kerkour-house-gucci-and-challenging-typecasting|url-status=live}}</ref> On January 4, 2022, Comer revealed her departure from the film due to [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on cinema|scheduling changes caused by the COVID-19 pandemic]] and described the situation as "rubbish".<ref name="ComerJanuary2022">{{Cite web|last=Kit|first=Borys|date=January 4, 2022|title=Jodie Comer Exits Ridley Scott's Napoleon Drama ''Kitbag'' (Exclusive)|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/jodie-comer-exits-ridley-scott-kitbag-movie-1235069264/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220104210630/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/jodie-comer-exits-ridley-scott-kitbag-movie-1235069264/|archive-date=January 4, 2022|access-date=January 4, 2022|website=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> [[Vanessa Kirby]] was announced as her replacement later that day.<ref name="KirbyJanuary2022">{{cite web |last1=Grobar |first1=Matt |title=Ridley Scott Chooses Vanessa Kirby To Play Josephine Opposite Joaquin Phoenix's Napoleon in Apple Epic ''Kitbag'' |url=https://deadline.com/2022/01/kitbag-vanessa-kirby-joaquin-phoenix-ridley-scott-napoleon-apple-replace-jodie-comer-1234904510/ |website=Deadline Hollywood |access-date=January 4, 2022 |date=January 4, 2022 |archive-date=January 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220104235509/https://deadline.com/2022/01/kitbag-vanessa-kirby-joaquin-phoenix-ridley-scott-napoleon-apple-replace-jodie-comer-1234904510/ |url-status=live}}</ref> On January 18, 2022, producer [[Kevin J. Walsh]] said the film had been retitled ''Napoleon''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2022/01/kevin-walsh-moves-scott-free-president-to-apple-production-deal-1234912124/|title=Kevin Walsh Moves From Scott Free Prexy to Multi-Year Apple TV+ Producing Deal|date=January 18, 2022|first=Mike Jr.|last=Fleming|website=Deadline Hollywood|access-date=January 18, 2022|archive-date=June 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220609012203/https://deadline.com/2022/01/kevin-walsh-moves-scott-free-president-to-apple-production-deal-1234912124/|url-status=live}}</ref> In February, [[Tahar Rahim]] was added to the cast, in the role of [[Paul Barras]].<ref name="Rahim">{{cite web |last1=Kroll |first1=Justin |title=''The Serpent'' Star Tahar Rahim Joins Joaquin Phoenix In Apple And Ridley Scott's ''Napoleon'' |url=https://deadline.com/2022/02/the-serpent-tahar-rahim-joaquin-phoenix-apple-ridley-scotts-napoleon-1234935281/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=February 16, 2022 |date=February 16, 2022 |archive-date=March 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220310195449/https://deadline.com/2022/02/the-serpent-tahar-rahim-joaquin-phoenix-apple-ridley-scotts-napoleon-1234935281/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The historian Lorris Chevalier, who worked on ''The Last Duel'', became the historical advisor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chevalier |first=Lorris |date=October 16, 2023 |title=Bertrandon de la Broquière: A Medieval Secret Agent? |url=https://www.medievalists.net/2023/10/bertrandon-de-la-broquiere-a-medieval-secret-agent/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231102211052/https://www.medievalists.net/2023/10/bertrandon-de-la-broquiere-a-medieval-secret-agent/ |archive-date=November 2, 2023 |access-date=October 24, 2023 |website=Medievalists.net |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Filming===
{{Multiple image
| total_width       = 500
| image1            = Lincoln Cathedral.jpg
| alt1              = The West Front of Lincoln Cathedral seen from the Castle wall in 2006.
| caption1          = Initial filming took place at [[Lincoln Cathedral]].
| image2            = Blenheim Palace 6-2008 4.jpg

Production began in February 2022.<ref name="Rahim" /> The film features six major battle sequences, unlike ''[[Waterloo (1970 film)|Waterloo]]'' (1970), another film featuring Napoleon, that focused on a single battle.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/video/ridley-scott-behind-the-lens/|title=Ridley Scott On ''House Of Gucci'', ''The Last Duel'', Upcoming Napoleon And ''Gladiator'' Epics, And Why He Just Keeps Going – Behind The Lens|date=December 31, 2021|first=Pete|last=Hammond|website=Deadline Hollywood|access-date=January 1, 2022|archive-date=August 28, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220828045817/https://deadline.com/video/ridley-scott-behind-the-lens/|url-status=live}}</ref> The battles featured in the film are the [[Siege of Toulon (1793)|siege of Toulon]], [[Battle of the Pyramids]], [[Battle of Marengo]], [[Battle of Austerlitz]], [[Battle of Borodino]], and [[Battle of Waterloo]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Bentz |first=Adam |date=October 6, 2023 |title=How Many Of Napoleon's 66 Career Battles Are In Ridley Scott's Movie Revealed |url=https://screenrant.com/napoleon-movie-battles-how-many-comparison-real-life/ |access-date=October 6, 2023 |website=Screen Rant}}</ref> The Battle of Marengo sequence was removed from the theatrical cut but was retained in the director's cut.<ref>{{cite web |last=Vlessing |first=Etan |date=August 29, 2024 |title=Ridley Scott's 'Napoleon: The Director's Cut' Debuts on Apple TV+ |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/ridley-scotts-napoleon-the-directors-apple-tv-1235986970/ |access-date=August 29, 2024 |website=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref>

''Napoleon'' was shot under the working title ''Marengo'', a reference to the [[Battle of Marengo]] (1800).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thelincolnite.co.uk/2022/03/movie-set-at-lincoln-cathedral-continues-to-expand-ahead-of-napoleon-filming-this-week/|title=Movie set at Lincoln Cathedral continues to expand ahead of Napoleon filming this week|date=March 14, 2022|first=Ellis|last=Karran|website=The Lincolnite|access-date=March 14, 2022|archive-date=May 28, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220528095929/https://thelincolnite.co.uk/2022/03/movie-set-at-lincoln-cathedral-continues-to-expand-ahead-of-napoleon-filming-this-week/|url-status=usurped}}</ref> Filming took place in Lincoln, England in March 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thelincolnite.co.uk/2021/11/hollywood-filmmaker-ridley-scott-casting-for-new-movie-in-lincoln-starring-joaquin-phoenix/|title=Hollywood filmmaker Ridley Scott casting for new movie in Lincoln starring Joaquin Phoenix|date=November 26, 2021|first=Joseph|last=Verney|website=The Lincolnite|access-date=November 26, 2021|archive-date=March 31, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220331120756/https://thelincolnite.co.uk/2021/11/hollywood-filmmaker-ridley-scott-casting-for-new-movie-in-lincoln-starring-joaquin-phoenix/|url-status=usurped}}</ref> The crew reportedly spent a week to prepare [[Lincoln Cathedral]], which stood in for [[Notre-Dame de Paris]]. Shooting took place in the cathedral on March 17 and 18, between 7{{nbsp}}am to 7{{nbsp}}pm.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lincolnshire.gov.uk/news/article/958/napoleon-filming-set-to-start-soon|title=Napoleon filming set to start soon|date=March 2, 2022|publisher=Lincolnshire County Council|access-date=March 6, 2022|archive-date=March 3, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220303150044/https://www.lincolnshire.gov.uk/news/article/958/napoleon-filming-set-to-start-soon|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://thelincolnite.co.uk/2022/03/lincoln-cathedral-plays-role-of-notre-dame-on-napoleon-film-set/|title=Lincoln Cathedral plays role of Notre Dame on Napoleon film set|date=March 11, 2022|first=Ellis|last=Karran|website=The Lincolnite|access-date=March 17, 2022|archive-date=May 26, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220526174908/https://thelincolnite.co.uk/2022/03/lincoln-cathedral-plays-role-of-notre-dame-on-napoleon-film-set/|url-status=usurped}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://thelincolnite.co.uk/2022/03/watch-joaquin-phoenix-and-ridley-scott-spotted-at-lincoln-cathedral-during-napoleon-filming/|title=Watch: Joaquin Phoenix and Ridley Scott spotted at Lincoln Cathedral during Napoleon filming|date=March 18, 2022|first=Ellis|last=Karran|website=The Lincolnite|access-date=April 1, 2022|archive-date=March 31, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220331120811/https://thelincolnite.co.uk/2022/03/watch-joaquin-phoenix-and-ridley-scott-spotted-at-lincoln-cathedral-during-napoleon-filming/|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

{{Main|Napoleon (soundtrack){{!}}''Napoleon'' (soundtrack)}}

==Release==
''Napoleon'' premiered at [[Salle Pleyel]] in Paris on November 14, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2023/film/global/napoleon-paris-premiere-apple-sony-french-windowing-1235790441/|title=Ridley Scott's 'Napoleon' World Premieres in Paris With Joaquin Phoenix, Vanessa Kirby|work=Variety|first=Elsa|last=Keslassy|date=November 14, 2023|access-date=November 20, 2023|archive-date=November 20, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231120160844/https://variety.com/2023/film/global/napoleon-paris-premiere-apple-sony-french-windowing-1235790441/|url-status=live}}</ref> For the film's theatrical release, [[Apple Original Films]] partnered with [[Sony Pictures Releasing]], under their [[Columbia Pictures]] banner, to help exhibit the film worldwide.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2023/04/ridley-scott-napoleon-apple-joaquin-phoenix-november-22-sony-theatrical-release-1235316475/|title=Ridley Scott-Helmed 'Napoleon' Set By Apple Original Films For November Sony Theatrical Release; Let The Fall Fest Jockeying Begin!|website=Deadline|first=Mike Jr.|last=Fleming|date=April 3, 2023|access-date=July 12, 2023|archive-date=June 29, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230629041010/https://deadline.com/2023/04/ridley-scott-napoleon-apple-joaquin-phoenix-november-22-sony-theatrical-release-1235316475/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1247480/ridley-scott-napoleon-release-date-cast-more/ |last1=Brady |first1=Erin |last2=Ettenhofer |first2=Valerie |title=Ridley Scott's Napoleon - Release Date, Cast, Plot, Trailer, And More Info |website=[[/Film]] |access-date=October 22, 2023 |date=August 7, 2023 |archive-date=November 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231104172949/https://www.slashfilm.com/1247480/ridley-scott-napoleon-release-date-cast-more/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Poisuo |first=Pauli |title=Napoleon First Trailer Debuts Ridley Scott's Brutish Emperor On The Battlefield |url=https://www.looper.com/1299676/apple-tv-napoleon-movie-first-trailer/ |website=[[Looper (website)|Looper]] |access-date=October 22, 2023 |date=July 10, 2023 |archive-date=November 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231104172920/https://www.looper.com/1299676/apple-tv-napoleon-movie-first-trailer/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="THRreview">{{cite web |last=Rooney |first=David |title='Napoleon' Review: Joaquin Phoenix and Vanessa Kirby Get Bogged Down in the Battles of Ridley Scott's Historical Epic |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-reviews/napoleon-review-joaquin-phoenix-vanessa-kirby-ridley-scott-1235647400/ |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation]] |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=November 14, 2023 |archive-date=November 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116013716/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-reviews/napoleon-review-joaquin-phoenix-vanessa-kirby-ridley-scott-1235647400/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was released in cinemas first in the United States and the United Kingdom on November 22, 2023. In August 2023, Ridley Scott revealed that he had planned a director's cut of ''Napoleon'' that explored more of Empress Joséphine, and hoped that he would be able to release it in theaters and on Apple TV+, after the initial theatrical release.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/ridley-scott-napoleon-directors-cut-four-and-a-half-hours-1234901302/|title=Ridley Scott Teases a 'Fantastic' Four-and-a-Half Hour Director's Cut of 'Napoleon' with More Vanessa Kirby|last=Zilko|first=Christian|website=[[IndieWire]]|date=September 3, 2023|access-date=September 5, 2023|archive-date=September 4, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904081319/https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/ridley-scott-napoleon-directors-cut-four-and-a-half-hours-1234901302/|url-status=live}}</ref> Scott indicated that the director's cut would run four hours and ten minutes.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fuster |first=Jeremy |date=October 8, 2023 |title=Ridley Scott Says His 4-Hour 'Napoleon' Director's Cut Will Be Released on Apple TV+ |url=https://www.thewrap.com/napoleon-ridley-scott-directors-cut-streaming/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231009103629/https://www.thewrap.com/napoleon-ridley-scott-directors-cut-streaming/ |archive-date=October 9, 2023 |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=The Wrap}}</ref>

===Home media===

''Napoleon'' was released on digital platforms on January 9, 2024,<ref>{{cite web |last=Felt |first=Klein |date=January 4, 2024 |title=Napoleon Movie Online Release Date Revealed: When Will It Start Streaming? |url=https://thedirect.com/article/napoleon-movie-streaming-release-date-online |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240108072838/https://thedirect.com/article/napoleon-movie-streaming-release-date-online |archive-date=January 8, 2024 |access-date=January 8, 2024 |website=The Direct}}</ref> before streaming on March 1, 2024 on Apple TV+.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/ridley-scott-joaquin-phoenix-napoleon-movie-theatrical-release-date-apple-tv-debut-1235571909/|title=Ridley Scott, Joaquin Phoenix Epic 'Napoleon' Gets Exclusive Theatrical Release Before Apple TV+ Debut|website=Variety|first=Brent|last=Lang|date=April 3, 2023|access-date=April 3, 2023|archive-date=April 3, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230403180136/https://variety.com/2023/film/news/ridley-scott-joaquin-phoenix-napoleon-movie-theatrical-release-date-apple-tv-debut-1235571909/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pedersen |first=Erik |date=2024-02-15 |title='Napoleon' Streaming Campaign Gets Start Date On Apple TV+ |url=https://deadline.com/2024/02/napoleon-streaming-date-apple-tv-1235826716/ |access-date=2024-02-16 |website=Deadline}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Napoleon |url=https://www.apple.com/tv-pr/originals/napoleon/ |access-date=2024-03-01 |website=Apple TV+ Press |language=en-US}}</ref> 
On August 29, 2024, the director's cut was released on streaming with an additional 48 minutes of footage.<ref name="Tingley">{{cite web |first=Anna |last=Tingley |url=https://variety.com/2024/shopping/news/napoleon-directors-cut-release-apple-tv-1236123994/ |title='Napoleon: The Director's Cut,' Featuring 48 Minutes of Unseen Footage, Is Now Streaming on Apple TV+ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=August 29, 2024 |access-date=August 29, 2024 |archive-date=August 29, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240829174350/https://variety.com/2024/shopping/news/napoleon-directors-cut-release-apple-tv-1236123994/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Reception==
=== Box office ===
''Napoleon'' grossed $61.5&nbsp;million in the United States and Canada, and $160.9&nbsp;million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $222.4&nbsp;million.<ref name="NUM" /><ref name="BOM" /> In February 2024, ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' reported that this gross fell short of covering the film's marketing budget, with revenues falling about $16 million behind. This shortfall was made up by home rentals, but according to the publication that still left an estimated loss of around $165 million, equivalent to the production budget, for Apple.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/02/box-office-argylle-1235812281/ |title= Argylle' With C+ CinemaScore & $18M Opening Crashes: Can Apple Sustain This Reign Of $200M Productions? – Sunday Update |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=February 4, 2024 |first=Anthony |last=D'Alessandro |access-date=February 4, 2024 |archive-date=February 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240203021723/https://deadline.com/2024/02/box-office-argylle-1235812281/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In contrast, Apple insisted the film was profitable.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/apple-box-office-misfires-napoleon-flower-moon-argylle-1235931957/ |title=Apple's Blockbuster Gamble: Was Spending $700 Million on 'Killers of the Flower Moon', 'Napoleon' and 'Argylle' Worth It? |first=Tatiana |last=Siegel |date=March 6, 2024 |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=June 3, 2024}}</ref>

In the United States and Canada, ''Napoleon'' was released alongside ''[[Wish (film)|Wish]]'' and the wide expansion of ''[[Saltburn (film)|Saltburn]]'', and was originally projected to gross around $22 million from 3,500 theaters over its five-day [[Thanksgiving (United States)|Thanksgiving]] opening weekend.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=D'Alessandro |first1=Anthony |first2=Nancy |last2=Tartaglione |date=November 20, 2023 |title='Wish' To Rise Disney Animation's Star Over Thanksgiving With $75M Global Opening; 'Napoleon' Charges For $46M WW – Box Office Preview |url=https://deadline.com/2023/11/wish-napoleon-box-office-thanksgiving-projection-1235630318/ |access-date=November 20, 2023 |website=Deadline Hollywood |archive-date=November 20, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231120233320/https://deadline.com/2023/11/wish-napoleon-box-office-thanksgiving-projection-1235630318/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After making $7.7 million on its first day (including $3 million from Tuesday night previews), estimates were raised to $29–33 million. It made $4.4 million on Thanksgiving Day and $8.4 million on Friday. The film went on to debut to $20.4 million in its opening weekend (and a total of $32.5 million over the five days), finishing second behind holdover ''[[The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes]]''.<ref name="opening">{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=November 26, 2023 |title='Songbirds & Snakes' Reigns Supreme Over Thanksgiving Stretch With $42M 5-day; 'Napoleon' Steps On Disney's 'Wish' With $32M+ — Box Office |url=https://deadline.com/2023/11/box-office-wish-napoleon-thanksgiving-1235634036/ |access-date=November 26, 2023 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en-US |archive-date=November 26, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126003448/https://deadline.com/2023/11/box-office-wish-napoleon-thanksgiving-1235634036/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It fell 65% in its second weekend to sixth place, grossing $7.1 million.<ref>{{cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |url=https://deadline.com/2023/12/box-office-renaissance-a-film-by-beyonce-godzilla-minus-one-hunger-games-1235647651/ |title='Renaissance: A Film By Beyoncé' $22M Opening Irreplaceable For Sleepy Early December Weekend; Fuels $95M+ Frame Best Post 2018 – Update |date=December 3, 2023 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=December 3, 2023 |archive-date=December 2, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231202172438/https://deadline.com/2023/12/box-office-renaissance-a-film-by-beyonce-godzilla-minus-one-hunger-games-1235647651/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Rebecca Rubin of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' noted that under a traditional theatrical release, the film would need to gross $500–600 million worldwide in order to [[break-even]] given its $200 million budget. However, the success of the film could not be based solely on the box office, and would hinge on subscribers driven to Apple TV+ and "on-demand rentals and other revenue streams that wouldn't have been possible by going directly to streaming". Stephen Galloway, dean of [[Dodge College of Film and Media Arts|Chapman University's film school]], stated: "Apple making a $200 million movie is like you buying a cup of coffee and spilling it, but it's not making their brand look good if films like ''[[Killers of the Flower Moon]]'' and ''Napoleon'' underperform at the box office."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rubin |first=Rebecca |date=November 7, 2023 |title='Killers of the Flower Moon' Box Office: Is Martin Scorsese's $200 Million Epic a Hit or Flop? |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/killers-of-the-flower-moon-box-office-martin-scorsese-hit-flop-1235783109/ |access-date=November 21, 2023 |website=Variety |archive-date=November 20, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231120175454/https://variety.com/2023/film/news/killers-of-the-flower-moon-box-office-martin-scorsese-hit-flop-1235783109/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Critical response ===
{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|58|6.2|342|Ridley Scott is intent on proving the emperor has no clothes in ''Napoleon'', a slyly funny epic with bravura set pieces and a divided runtime that keeps it from outright conquering.|access-date=November 18, 2024|ref=y}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 64 out of 100, based on 62 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''Napoleon'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/napoleon-2023 |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=March 11, 2024 |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status=}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B−" on an A+ to F scale, while those polled by [[PostTrak]] gave it a 72% overall positive score, with 46% saying they would definitely recommend the film.<ref name="opening" />

Critics praised the film's epic scale, battle scenes, and Phoenix and Kirby's performances, while some took issue with the length and Scott's "bloated" direction.<ref name="THR-reviews">{{cite web |last=Rahman |first=Abid |date=November 14, 2023 |title=Ridley Scott's 'Napoleon': What the Critics Are Saying |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/napoleon-review-roundup-what-the-critics-are-saying-1235647576/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231121180656/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/napoleon-review-roundup-what-the-critics-are-saying-1235647576/ |archive-date=November 21, 2023 |access-date=November 22, 2023 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref> French critics had a less enthusiastic view than those from Britain and America, considering ''Napoleon'' "lazy, pointless, boring, migraine-inducing, too short and historically inaccurate".<ref>{{cite web|first=Catherine|last=Porter|title=France Scoffs at an Englishman's 'Napoleon'|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/11/24/arts/french-critics-napoleon.html|website=The New York Times|date=November 24, 2023|access-date=November 25, 2023|archive-date=November 25, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231125084002/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/11/24/arts/french-critics-napoleon.html|url-status=live}}</ref> A review in ''[[Le Figaro]]'' stated that the film could have been called "[[Barbie]] and [[Ken (doll)|Ken]] under the Empire", and another in the French edition of ''[[GQ]]'' deemed it to be "deeply clumsy, unnatural and unintentionally funny".<ref name="frost"/> [[Patrice Gueniffey]], a leading historian in [[Napoleonic studies]], called the movie "anti-French and very pro-British" in an interview to ''[[Le Point]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 14, 2023 |title=Patrice Gueniffey : " "Napoléon", c'est le film d'un Anglais… très antifrançais " |trans-title=Patrice Gueniffey: "Napoléon" is the film of an Englishman... who is very anti-French". |url=https://www.lepoint.fr/culture/patrice-gueniffey-napoleon-c-est-le-film-d-un-anglais-tres-antifrancais-14-11-2023-2543097_3.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126162234/https://www.lepoint.fr/culture/patrice-gueniffey-napoleon-c-est-le-film-d-un-anglais-tres-antifrancais-14-11-2023-2543097_3.php |archive-date=November 26, 2023 |access-date=November 26, 2023 |website=Le Point |language=French}}</ref><ref name="razzall">{{Cite news |last=Razzall |first=Katie |date=November 19, 2023 |title=Napoleon's Ridley Scott on critics and cinema 'bum ache' |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-67419876 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231119135525/https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-67419876 |archive-date=November 19, 2023 |access-date=November 19, 2023 |work=BBC News}}</ref>

[[Kyle Smith (critic)|Kyle Smith]] of ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' stated that "Mr. Phoenix's ''Napoleon'' could never have commanded so much as a squadron of the [[The Salvation Army|Salvation Army]], and though the movie is sprinkled with a few reasonably hearty battle scenes, overall it's something like Mr. Scott's ''[[Waterloo (1970 film)|Waterloo]]''."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/film/napoleon-review-ridley-scott-joaquin-phoenix-france-bonaparte-vanessa-kirby-c9547205|title='Napoleon' Review: Ridley Scott's Caricature of a Conqueror}}</ref> In a one-and-a-half out of four review, Odie Henderson of ''[[The Boston Globe|Boston Globe]]'' said, "It relies far too often on the "little man, big temper" idea of ''Napoleon'' — at times, Phoenix is practically channeling an angry [[Donald Duck]] mid-meltdown — and the scenes between the two lovers make them seem more like robots emulating human beings."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2023/11/21/arts/napoleon-is-far-dynamite/|title='Napoleon' is far from dynamite}}</ref> Writing in ''[[The Guardian]]'', [[Peter Bradshaw]] gave the film a full five stars and called it a "thrilling biopic", concluding that Scott "doesn't withhold the old-fashioned pleasures of spectacle and excitement. Phoenix is the key to it all: a performance as robust as the glass of burgundy he knocks back: preening, brooding, seething and triumphing."<ref>{{cite web |last=Bradshaw |first=Peter |date=November 15, 2023 |title=Napoleon review – Joaquin Phoenix makes a magnificent emperor in thrilling biopic |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2023/nov/15/napoleon-review-joaquin-phoenix-emperor-ridley-scott |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231115062352/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2023/nov/15/napoleon-review-joaquin-phoenix-emperor-ridley-scott |archive-date=November 15, 2023 |accessdate=November 15, 2023 |website=The Guardian}}</ref> Writing in ''[[The Observer]]'', Wendy Ide gave it three out of five, calling it a "sturdy epic" that struggled to "show us what drove the military mastermind". She continued, "A man, even a man as combative as Napoleon, amounts to more than the battles he has fought. And it is in this respect that the film is less successful."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2023/nov/19/napoleon-review-ridley-scott-joaquin-phoenix-vanessa-kirby-josephine-bonaparte|accessdate=November 15, 2023|date=November 19, 2023|title=Napoleon review – Ridley Scott's sturdy epic only fully comes alive on the battlefield|first=Wendy|last=Ide|work=The Observer|archive-date=November 19, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231119100540/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2023/nov/19/napoleon-review-ridley-scott-joaquin-phoenix-vanessa-kirby-josephine-bonaparte|url-status=live}}</ref>
The [[BBC]]'s Nicholas Barber found the film's battle sequences "spectacular", and also praised the performances of Kirby and Phoenix.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barber |first=Nicholas |title=Napoleon review: Ridley Scott's biopic is 'an awe-inspiring achievement' |url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20231114-napoleon-review-ridley-scotts-biopic-is-an-awe-inspiring-achievement |access-date=November 16, 2023 |website=www.bbc.com |date=November 15, 2023 |language=en |archive-date=November 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116014234/https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20231114-napoleon-review-ridley-scotts-biopic-is-an-awe-inspiring-achievement |url-status=live }}</ref> Johnny Oleksinski of the ''[[New York Post]]'' wrote: "[...] it's too bad Scott could not deliver a brilliant character study of one of the world's great military leaders — and instead settled for letting a self-indulgent Phoenix fly over the cuckoo's nest".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oleksinski |first=Johnny |date=November 15, 2023 |title='Napoleon' review: Another Joaquin Phoenix looney tunes performance as Ridley Scott offers ho-hum biopic |url=https://nypost.com/2023/11/14/entertainment/napoleon-review-another-joaquin-phoenix-freak-show/ |access-date=November 16, 2023 |website=[[New York Post]] |language=en-US |archive-date=November 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116013028/https://nypost.com/2023/11/14/entertainment/napoleon-review-another-joaquin-phoenix-freak-show/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Time Out (magazine)|''Time Out'']]'s Phil de Semylen gave the film three out of five, writing that "Ridley Scott's beefy account of Napoleon's rise to power looks great, is served with some panache, but crucially lacks flavour."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.timeout.com/movies/napoleon-2023|title=Napoleon review: Ridley Scott delivers a spectacular but flavourless epic|first=Phil de|last=Semlyen|date=November 14, 2023|website=Time Out Worldwide|access-date=November 26, 2023|archive-date=November 26, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126140135/https://www.timeout.com/movies/napoleon-2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Historical accuracy==
[[File:Jacques-Louis David - The Coronation of Napoleon (1805-1807).jpg|thumb|upright=1.5|The film's [[Coronation of Napoleon|coronation]] scene is portrayed as it was depicted in the famous painting ''[[The Coronation of Napoleon]]'' by [[Jacques-Louis David]].]]
Many critics of the film's historical aspects, including historians [[Adam Tooze]] and [[Andrew Roberts, Baron Roberts of Belgravia|Andrew Roberts]], believed it ignored Napoleon's numerous non-military achievements, as well as his popularity with the French people.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Tooze |first1=Adam |last2=Abadi |first2=Cameron |date=December 1, 2023 |title=The Economic Legacy of Napoleon Bonaparte |url=https://foreignpolicy.com/2023/12/01/the-economic-legacy-of-napoleon-bonaparte/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231201221148/https://foreignpolicy.com/2023/12/01/the-economic-legacy-of-napoleon-bonaparte/ |archive-date=December 1, 2023 |access-date=December 2, 2023 |website=Foreign Policy}}</ref><ref name="times">{{Cite news |last=Roberts |first=Andrew |date=November 19, 2023 |title=How accurate is the Napoleon film? A historian sorts fact from fiction |url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/books/article/how-accurate-napoleon-film-fact-fiction-true-0jhnjq6xq |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231120173129/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/how-accurate-napoleon-film-fact-fiction-true-0jhnjq6xq |archive-date=November 20, 2023 |access-date=November 20, 2023 |newspaper=The Sunday Times}}</ref> Roberts, a Napoleon biographer, said his portrayal as a proto-[[Adolf Hitler|Hitler]] was "as tired as it is absurd".<ref name= "razzall"/><ref name="guardian">{{Cite news |last=Thorpe |first=Vanessa |date=November 25, 2023 |title=Critics of Napoleon epic have fallen for emperor's fibs, says film's military expert |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/nov/25/napoleon-film-ridley-scott-critics-miitary-expert-battle-scenes |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231125164944/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/nov/25/napoleon-film-ridley-scott-critics-miitary-expert-battle-scenes |archive-date=November 25, 2023 |access-date=November 25, 2023 |newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref> Historian Zack White agreed, arguing the film "swallowed old British propaganda" which depicted Napoleon as a "Corsican ruffian".<ref name = "guardian" /> Ellin Stein, writing for ''[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]'', pointed out that Napoleon was known for his passion for literature and [[Age of Enlightenment|Enlightenment]] thought – a far cry from the boorish, loutish soldier that Scott depicts.<ref name="slate">{{Cite web |last=Stein |first=Ellin |date=November 22, 2023 |title=What's Fact and What's Fiction in Napoleon |url=https://slate.com/culture/2023/11/napoleon-movie-ridely-scott-joaquin-phoenix-true-story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231127165804/https://slate.com/culture/2023/11/napoleon-movie-ridely-scott-joaquin-phoenix-true-story.html |archive-date=November 27, 2023 |access-date=November 27, 2023 |website=Slate}}</ref> French historian [[Patrice Gueniffey]] called the movie "anti-French" and full of historical inaccuracies, while fellow historian Romain Marsily found the portrayal of Napoleon "lackluster" and “mediocre” while disregarding Napoleon's positive legacies such as the [[Napoleonic Code]].<ref name="razzall" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bentz |first=Adam |date=December 7, 2023 |title=Napoleon's Historical Inaccuracies Called Out By French Historians: "A Big Disappointment" |url=https://screenrant.com/napoleon-movie-historical-inaccuracies-french-historians-response/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209155034/https://screenrant.com/napoleon-movie-historical-inaccuracies-french-historians-response/ |archive-date=December 9, 2023 |access-date=December 22, 2023 |website=[[Screen Rant]] |language=en}}</ref> Spanish historian Francisco Gracia Alonso called the film "a crime".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Gómez |first=Javier |date=December 5, 2023 |title=El Napoleón de Ridley Scott. Más que un error, un crimen |trans-title=Ridley Scott's Napoleon. More than a mistake, a crime |url=https://www.despertaferro-ediciones.com/2023/critica-pelicula-napoleon-ridley-scott-joaquin-phoenix/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240114031749/https://www.despertaferro-ediciones.com/2023/critica-pelicula-napoleon-ridley-scott-joaquin-phoenix/ |archive-date=January 14, 2024 |access-date=December 28, 2023 |website=Desperta Ferro Ediciones |language=es}}</ref> Historian Joan Tumblety wrote that the movie ignored French atrocities such as those committed after the [[Siege of Jaffa]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tumblety |first=Joan |date=November 17, 2023 |title=Did Napoleon really fire at the pyramids? A historian explains the truth behind the legends of Ridley Scott's biopic |url=https://theconversation.com/did-napoleon-really-fire-at-the-pyramids-a-historian-explains-the-truth-behind-the-legends-of-ridley-scotts-biopic-217951 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126191952/https://theconversation.com/did-napoleon-really-fire-at-the-pyramids-a-historian-explains-the-truth-behind-the-legends-of-ridley-scotts-biopic-217951 |archive-date=November 26, 2023 |access-date=November 26, 2023 |website=The Conversation}}</ref>

Napoleon did not attend the execution of [[Marie Antoinette]], as he was commanding forces at [[Siege of Toulon|Toulon]] at the time. The film additionally depicts a defeated Napoleon meeting Wellington, whereas in actuality, the two men never met.<ref name="quenoy">{{Cite web |author1=Quenoy |first=Paul du |date=November 26, 2023 |title=Ridley Scott's Napoleon Is an Unmitigated Disaster |url=https://europeanconservative.com/articles/reviews/ridley-scotts-napoleon-is-an-unmitigated-disaster/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128181118/https://europeanconservative.com/articles/reviews/ridley-scotts-napoleon-is-an-unmitigated-disaster/ |archive-date=November 28, 2023 |access-date=November 27, 2023 |website=The European Conservative}}</ref><ref name="fp">{{Cite web |last=Gady |first=Franz-Stefan |date=December 2, 2023 |title=Movie Review: What Ridley Scott's 'Napoleon' Gets Wrong About War |url=https://foreignpolicy.com/2023/12/02/napoleon-ridley-scott-review-movie-battle-military-historical-accuracy-myth/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240119122532/https://foreignpolicy.com/2023/12/02/napoleon-ridley-scott-review-movie-battle-military-historical-accuracy-myth/ |archive-date=January 19, 2024 |access-date=December 10, 2023 |website=Foreign Policy}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lang |first=Kevin |date=November 22, 2023 |title=Napoleon: History Vs. Hollywood |url=https://www.historyvshollywood.com/reelfaces/napoleon/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126003217/https://www.historyvshollywood.com/reelfaces/napoleon/ |archive-date=November 26, 2023 |access-date=November 26, 2023 |publisher=[[History vs. Hollywood]]}}</ref> [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] historian [[Michael Broers]], who worked on the movie, noted several inaccuracies in Napoleon and Josephine's relationship, including the timing of their divorce (1809, not 1807), its nature (Napoleon did not slap Josephine during their divorce), and its rationale (Josephine is portrayed as accepting the inevitability of the divorce, whereas in reality, she was fearful of it).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waxman |first=Olivia B. |date=November 22, 2023 |title=How Ridley Scott's 'Napoleon' Stacks Up Against the French Emperor's Real Story |url=https://time.com/6338563/napoleon-movie-true-story/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126001216/https://time.com/6338563/napoleon-movie-true-story/ |archive-date=November 26, 2023 |access-date=November 26, 2023 |publisher=TIME}}</ref> The historical Joséphine died in May 1814, a few weeks after Napoleon's exile to [[Elba]], rather than a year later during the [[Hundred Days]] as depicted in the film. Therefore, her illness or death was not a direct factor in Napoleon's escape and return to France.<ref name="quenoy" />

The film presents Napoleon as firing on the [[Giza pyramid complex|Pyramids of Giza]], which never happened.<ref name="slate" /> Cairo [[Egyptologist]] [[Salima Ikram]] pointed out that Napoleon held the [[Great Sphinx of Giza|Sphinx]] and the pyramids in high esteem and used them as motivation for his troops. "He definitely did not take pot shots at them."<ref>{{Cite web |author1=Ferreira |first=Becky |date=November 22, 2023 |title=Napoleon Didn't Really Shoot Cannons at Egypt's Pyramids |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/11/22/science/napoleon-movie-ridley-scott-egypt-pyramid.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126191952/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/11/22/science/napoleon-movie-ridley-scott-egypt-pyramid.html |archive-date=November 26, 2023 |access-date=November 26, 2023 |website=The New York Times}}</ref> In an interview with ''[[The Times]]'', Scott defended his depiction of the attack on the pyramids as being "a fast way of saying [Napoleon] took Egypt".<ref name="The Times">{{Cite news |author1=Dean |first=Jonathan |date=November 12, 2023 |title=Ridley Scott: I didn't need historians to make my Napoleon epic |url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/film/article/ridley-scott-i-didnt-listen-to-historians-to-make-my-napoleon-epic-snq5f7x68 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260220110835/https://www.thetimes.com/culture/film/article/ridley-scott-i-didnt-listen-to-historians-to-make-my-napoleon-epic-snq5f7x68 |archive-date=February 20, 2026 |access-date=November 26, 2023 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref>

Major events of Napoleon's reign such as the [[Peninsular War]], the [[Saint-Domingue expedition]], the [[Haitian Revolution]], the [[War of the Fifth Coalition|Austrian campaign of 1809]] and the [[War of the Sixth Coalition|campaigns of 1813 and 1814]] are entirely omitted. The depiction of the [[Battle of Waterloo]] silences the roles of Dutch and German armies. Napoleon's [[Marshal of the Empire|marshals]], who played a key role in his campaigns, are almost entirely absent.<ref name=":0" /> The film was criticized for ignoring Napoleon's decision to [[Law of 20 May 1802|reinstate slavery]] in France's [[French colonial empire|overseas colonies]] in 1802 after it had been abolished by the National Convention following the French Revolution.<ref name="variety-napoleon">{{Cite web |last=Keslassy |first=Elsa |date=December 6, 2023 |title=French Historians Slam Ridley Scott's 'Napoleon' Inaccuracies: 'Like Spitting in the Face of French People' |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/napoleon-inaccuracies-french-historians-pyramids-1235823975/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231216070702/https://variety.com/2023/film/news/napoleon-inaccuracies-french-historians-pyramids-1235823975/ |archive-date=December 16, 2023 |access-date=December 19, 2023 |website=Variety}}</ref>

Historian [[Paul du Quenoy]] criticized the depiction of Napoleonic era [[Napoleonic tactics|battlefield tactics]], especially the [[Battle of Austerlitz|Austerlitz]] sequence, "one of the few battles that the film depicts in detail". He noted that historians consider the ambush on the ice to be a myth of the [[Ulm campaign|Austerlitz campaign]], "a minor detail whose significance has been doubted almost since the time of the battle".<ref name="quenoy" /> Napoleon, an artillery officer by training, never personally led a [[Charge (warfare)|cavalry charge]], as is shown at [[Battle of Borodino|Borodino]] and [[Battle of Waterloo|Waterloo]].<ref name="fp" /><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Cremona |first1=Patrick |last2=Moss |first2=Molly |date=November 29, 2023 |title=Napoleon true story: How accurate is the historical epic? |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/napoleon-true-story/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128093812/https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/napoleon-true-story/ |archive-date=November 28, 2023 |access-date=November 27, 2023 |website=Radio Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Diggins |first1=Alex |date=November 24, 2023 |title=Fact-checking Napoleon: how accurate is Ridley Scott's film? |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/2023/11/24/napoleon-fact-vs-fiction-joaquin-phoenix-ridley-scott/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126191952/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/2023/11/24/napoleon-fact-vs-fiction-joaquin-phoenix-ridley-scott/ |archive-date=November 26, 2023 |access-date=November 26, 2023 |newspaper=The Telegraph}}</ref> Franz-Stefan Gady, writing for ''[[Foreign Policy]]'', described the battle sequences as "a Hollywood mishmash of medieval melees, meaningless cannonades, and [[World War I]]-style [[infantry]] advances". "For all of Scott’s fixation on Napoleon’s battles, he seems curiously disinterested in how the real Napoleon fought them."<ref name="fp" />

Scott dismissed criticisms of these historical inaccuracies, saying, "Napoleon dies then, ten years later, someone writes a book. Then someone takes that book and writes another, and so, 400 [sic] years later, there's a lot of imagination [in history books]. When I have issues with historians, I ask: 'Excuse me, mate, were you there? No? Well, shut the f*** up then.' "<ref name="The Times"/><ref name="frost">{{Cite web |author=Caroline Frost |date=November 19, 2023 |title='Napoleon' Director Ridley Scott Dismisses Critics: "The French Don't Even Like Themselves |url=https://deadline.com/2023/11/napoleon-director-ridley-scott-dismisses-critics-epic-film-joaquin-phoenix-1235627199/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231119135523/https://deadline.com/2023/11/napoleon-director-ridley-scott-dismisses-critics-epic-film-joaquin-phoenix-1235627199/ |archive-date=November 19, 2023 |access-date=November 19, 2023 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> Scott also declared, responding to French critics, that "the French don't even like themselves".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharf |first=Zack |date=November 20, 2023 |title=Ridley Scott Tells Off French Critics Who Dislike 'Napoleon': 'The French Don't Even Like Themselves' |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/ridley-scott-slams-french-napoleon-reviews-1235801660/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231201022012/https://variety.com/2023/film/news/ridley-scott-slams-french-napoleon-reviews-1235801660/ |archive-date=December 1, 2023 |access-date=December 2, 2023 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>
